title: LISTA router for Mirror atom coefficients
hypothesis: A learned fixed-depth LISTA inference network on the same shared functional dictionary will approach OMP sparse-code reconstruction with lower inference steps, while its serialized router weights remain smaller than the per-function dense coefficient representation.
mirror_coordinate: input-specific sparse atom coefficients inferred by OMP or a trained LISTA network
logical_multiplicity: function-specific sparse combinations from shared atoms
controls: OMP sparse codes on same dictionary and top-8 budget

metrics: serialized router + dictionary + function codes bytes

development.allowed: train LISTA on development examples only; fixed top-8 sparsity and predeclared 1/2/4/8 steps; no fresh-dependent changes

paid_objects: per-function inputs or sparse codes as required by inference contract

success_gate: At <=8 LISTA steps, every fresh bank has NRMSE <=0.05 and <=1.05x OMP top-8 error; router compute/bytes are reported and end-to-end inference beats OMP on measured latency or MAC.
failure_gate: LISTA misses quality, requires more compute/bytes than OMP without offsetting inference benefit, or router is only evaluated on training functions.
boundaries: Synthetic fixed dictionary and sparse-vector task; no neural MoE routing claim.
LISTA training examples are development only; fresh target functions are unseen.
Do not interpret number of sparse combinations as capacity.
